sentences.text: By way of the instant petition, the petitioner is challenging the selection and appointment of respondent No. 4 on the post of Assistant Grade III by the respondent authorities.

2. Brief facts of the case as mentioned in the petition are that the respondent No. 2 is a registered body in the name of Raipur Dioceses Educational Society, Raipur bearing registration No. 5261 dated 27-01-1977, Head Office at Khrist Bandhu Niwas Byran Bazar Raipur.

entities.text: Khrist Bandhu Niwas Byran Bazar Raipur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Vide Annexure P/3 dated 03.01.2013, respondent No. 2 gave the names of executive members of the society u/s 27 of C.G. Society Registration Act, 1973.
Respondent No. 2 was running one of the schools situated at Bilaspur Knows Bharatmata Hindi Medium Higher Secondary School situated at Railway market road Bilaspur.

entities.text: Bharatmata Hindi Medium Higher Secondary School
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said school is a non-govt. grant aided school and was under the control of respondent No. 3.

The selection on vacant post is to be done as per Rules prescribed under M.P.C.G.
Non Govt. Education Society (ADHYAPAKO TATHA ANYA KERMCHARIYO KE BHARTI) Rule,
1979.
3.

entities.text:
M.P.C.G.

1979
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 31.01.2014, Secretary of Bharatmata Hindi Medium H.S. School Bilaspur (C.G.) published an advertisement (Annexure P/4) through newspaper for appointment and selection on the post of Assistant Grade III.

entities.text: Bharatmata Hindi Medium H.S. School Bilaspur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the said advertisement, the category for the said post was not mentioned.
Advertisement dated 31.01.2014 was not published by the authority.
Appointing authority is the Director of the society and every vacant post ought to be appointed by respondent No. 2 through Director.

4. The petitioner was appointed as Upper Division Clerk at Bharatmata Hindi Medium Hr. Sec.
School (RS) Bilaspur by respondent No. 2 from 01-11-2010 to 01-11-2012 on Adhoc basis.

entities.text:
Bharatmata Hindi Medium Hr. Sec.
School (RS) Bilaspur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
A copy of appointment order filed as Annexure P/5 to P/7.
5.

Respondent No. 2 arbitrary and illegally appointed respondent No.4 as the said appointment is not as per Rule of M.P./C.G. non govt. Education Society (ADHYAPAKO TATHA ANYA KERMCHARIYO KE BHARTI) Rule 1979.

entities.text: M.P./C.G. non govt. Education Society (ADHYAPAKO TATHA ANYA KERMCHARIYO KE BHARTI) Rule 1979
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 did not follow the proper procedure in appointing the respondent No.4 for the said post and also did not publish the advertisement in common newspaper and notice board of school.
Therefore, the petitioner did not know about the publication of the said vacant post and she was debarred froml applying for the same due to arbitrary act of respondent No. 2.
the petitioner is a handicapped lady and wanted to apply for the said post as she worked as a clerk in the said school.

2 6.

entities.text: Freeda Mary vs State Of Chhattisgarh And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioner filed complaint before respondent No. 3 on 17.02.2014 (Annexure P/8) about illegal selection of respondent No. 4 but no action was taken by respondent No. 3.
Thereafter, 27.04.2015 (Annexure P/9), she filed another complaint before the Collector Bilaspur but of no avail.

Hence, this petition has been filed by the petitioner for following reliefs:-
"10.1
The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to call for the entire records pertaining to this case from possession of the respondents for its kind perusal.

10.2 The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue a writ in the nature of mandamus or suitable direction to the respondents to take proper inquiry about the selection of respondent No.4 and cancel the selection of the respondent No.4 for the post of Asst. clerk grade 3.
10.3
Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper may also be passed in favour of the petitioner."

7. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that respondent No. 2 illegally and arbitrary and by taking personal interest and without properly publishing the said post in common daily newspaper,
appointed respondent No. 4 on the vacant post of Assistant Grade III.
Respondent No. 2 did not follow the rules under Section 9(2) of M.P.C.G. Ashaskiya Shikshan Sanstha (Adhyapakon Tatha Anya Karmachariyon Ki Bharti) Niyam, 1979.

entities.text: M.P.C.G. Ashaskiya Shikshan Sanstha (Adhyapakon Tatha Anya Karmachariyon Ki Bharti) Niyam, 1979
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Advertisement was not published by proper appointing authority.
Respondent No. 2 did not provide any information to employment office about the vacancy of the above post in school as per rule 9(4) of the above Act.
The selection committee was not properly constituted as per Rule 12 of the above Act.

Therefore, the record of respondent No.4 may be called and respondents No. 1 to 3 may be directed to conduct proper enquiry regarding selection of respondent No. 4 and cancel the appointment of respondent No.4 on the post of Assistant Grade III.

8. Learned counsel for respondent No.1/State submits that respondents No. 2 and 3 are employer of respondent No.4 and State is a formal party in the instant petition and since no substantial and effective relief has been sought by the petitioner against the answering respondent, therefore, the instant petition is liable to be dismissed.
9. Respondents No. 2 to 4 did not file any return/reply to this petition.
10. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
11.

Petitioner also filed additional document on 05.08.2024 and on perusal of the said document it appears that FIR No. 0192 of 2024 has been lodged against respondent No.4 and another accused person for the offence under Section 420, 34 of IPC.
12.
It is evident on perusal of document (Annexure P/1) that except the signature of the principal,
signatures
of other members and president were not there.

Freeda Mary vs State Of Chhattisgarh And Ors on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174839528/
3 13.

entities.text: Freeda Mary vs State Of Chhattisgarh And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner filed complaint against respondent No.4 but respondents No.2 and 3 did not consider the said complaint.
Respondent No.1 is Secretary, School & Shisha Department and also did not file any reply in this petition.
On perusal of Annexure P/1 dated 16.02.2014 and FIR, it is clear that the appointment of respondent No.4 is not in accordance with rules and regulations.

14. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and material available on record, this petition stands disposed of with direction to respondents No. 1 to 3 to conduct proper enquiry regarding appointment of respondent No.4 after giving proper opportunity of hearing to respondent No.4.
This exercise must be completed as early as possible preferably within a period of six months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

15. If it is found in enquiry that the appointment of respondent No.4 is not made in accordance with rules and regulations, then proper action shall be taken against all those persons who were responsible for the said irregularities done in the selection and appointment process of respondent No.4.
16.
Registry is directed to send copy of this order to the concerned respondent authorities for necessary information and compliance of this order.

Sd/-
 (Rajani Dubey)
 JUDGE  Ruchi RUCHI YADAV RUCHI YADAV Freeda Mary vs State Of Chhattisgarh And Ors on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174839528/
